summary: Intermittent long tail inference delays: customer reports requests perceived as 'hung' but backend returning soft-429s; client retries amplifying load
description:
Issue summary:
CuraSense reports intermittent requests that appear to 'hang' or return after tens of seconds. Customer observes wide tail latency spikes correlated to heavy traffic windows. They see client-side timeouts/retries and believe the serving runtime is slowing.

Impact:
- Several production customers of CuraSense saw elevated tail latency (p95->p99) during morning batch runs; product features that rely on sub-second responses degrade.
- Customer experienced increased error counts and duplicate charges from retries.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (prod-us-east) running dedicated pool for CuraSense.
- Customer uses SDK-js v1.3.6 with default retry policy.
- Affected model: redwood/rhine-13b-8k pinned at v2026-02-28.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Run 120 concurrent streaming requests with 1–2 token priming across 10 hosts from us-east ip range.
2) Observe ~3–8% of requests take >10s or appear to never return to the client (client eventually times out and retries).
3) Client logs show rapid immediate retries after perceived timeout; server logs show bursts of 429s.

Observed behavior:
- Server logs show many short-lived 429 responses (soft quota enforcement) with no Retry-After header present in most cases.
- Client SDK immediately retries on socket timeout/closed stream without exponential jitter. This creates retry amplification and increases load on the rate limiter, which in turn produces more 429 responses (feedback loop).

Expected behavior:
- Soft quota 429s should be communicated with Retry-After or gracefully degrade (503) so clients back off.
- SDK should implement exponential backoff + jitter and treat 429s as explicit signals to back off.

Relevant logs & links:
- Trace samples: trace ids: trace-20260310-7cf8b1, trace-20260310-7cf8d2 (linked to internal trace store)
- Rate limiter dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rate-limiter/soft-quota-bursts
- Customer's SDK logs (attached in ticket)

investigation_notes: SRE reproduction: under sustained short-request concurrency the api-gateway's token-bucket enters a soft-quota state and begins returning 429s to some requests in microbursts.

Many 429 responses lacked Retry-After header due to codepath in legacy rate-limiter (relevant service: rate-limiter v2.4.1) that returns 429 in soft-deny mode without adding Retry-After. This makes it a non-explicit signal to clients.
Observed client behavior: SDK-js v1.3.6 treats socket close/timeouts as transient and retries immediately up to N attempts with no jitter; combined with short timeouts this amplifies traffic.
Correlation shows retry storms align with p99 latency spikes and increased 429 counts; root cause is interaction between soft quota enforcement and aggressive client retries (amplification).
Proposed server-side fixes: add Retry-After header for soft-429s, consider returning 503 for short cooldown with Retry-After, enable burst-smoothing and token refill tuning for dedicated pools.
Proposed client-side fixes: release SDK patch to honor 429 as a backoff signal, implement exponential backoff + jitter, and add configurable max-concurrency defaults for short streaming workloads.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 - Short-term mitigation: increased CuraSense soft quota by 25% for next 72 hours and enabled api-gateway rate-smoothing. Observed immediate reduction in tail latency during customer morning window.
2026-03-13 - Server fix (PR #1428) merged: rate-limiter now sets Retry-After header on soft-429s and exposes per-customer cooldown metric. Rolling out to prod-us-east.
2026-03-13 - SDK fix (PR #329) merged: sdk-js v1.3.7 will interpret 429s as backoff signals and uses exponential backoff with jitter; released to npm and sent customer patch instructions.

Follow-up actions: schedule postmortem and add runbook entry: 'Handling soft quota 429s' in Confluence; update dedicated pool autoscaling knobs to reduce soft-deny frequency; coordinate SDK minor release notes and notify customers about recommended concurrency settings.
Customer verified: CuraSense reported improved p99 behavior after mitigations and agreed to onboard SDK patch across clients.
